implementation_issues.description: The 1964–2007 period is reported for the predictive regressions/major variables, while CRASH and NCSKEW are t+1 outcomes and crash-risk measurement extends 12 months through three months after the fiscal-year-end. The initial CRSP–Compustat draw ends in 2007 and the paper says 2007 is its predictive-regression cutoff. The exact regression-year versus outcome-year convention and resulting final raw dates are unresolved; retain unknown upper endpoints for future-risk inputs.

The exact weekly return aggregation boundaries and fiscal-year mapping are not given. The expanded market model uses market-index leads/lags up to two weeks, and the source requires at least 26 weekly returns per fiscal year. Daily DSF/DSI fields are present, but a week-construction convention remains necessary.

The paper specifies a CRSP–Compustat intersection but not the CCM primary-link/type/overlap selection rule. CCM supplies candidate effective-dated identifiers; exact target-population linking remains unresolved.

The MB market-to-book ratio is not fully defined by numerator, denominator, adjustments or timing. The source also gives both beginning-year CSCORE characteristics and fiscal-year control definitions; the regression text says controls are at the beginning of t. An exact MB construction and alignment must be resolved.
The selected firm-fixed-effects baseline fit is reported, but the estimator used for that FE fit is not identified; OLS is specified only for comparison without firm fixed effects.

The paper’s Table 1 control definitions and the equation text differ on control timing: Table notes label most controls in fiscal year t, while the prose says all controls are measured at the beginning of year t. The temporal audit uses the explicit beginning-of-year statement for those controls and preserves the conflict.
Use current Compustat/CRSP vintages for the original paper period. Restated accounting fields, identifier histories and return-adjustment conventions may differ from the authors’ source vintage.

implementation_issues.description: The 1964–2007 period is reported for the predictive regressions/major variables, while CRASH and NCSKEW are t+1 outcomes and crash-risk measurement extends 12 months through three months after the fiscal-year-end. The initial CRSP–Compustat draw ends in 2007 and the paper says 2007 is its predictive-regression cutoff. The exact regression-year versus outcome-year convention and resulting final raw dates are unresolved; retain unknown upper endpoints for future-risk inputs.

The exact weekly return aggregation boundaries and fiscal-year mapping are not given. The expanded market model uses market-index leads/lags up to two weeks, and the source requires at least 26 weekly returns per fiscal year. Daily DSF/DSI fields are present, but a week-construction convention remains necessary.

The paper specifies a CRSP–Compustat intersection but not the CCM primary-link/type/overlap selection rule. CCM supplies candidate effective-dated identifiers; exact target-population linking remains unresolved.

The MB market-to-book ratio is not fully defined by numerator, denominator, adjustments or timing. implementation_issues.description: The 1964–2007 period is reported for the predictive regressions/major variables, while CRASH and NCSKEW are t+1 outcomes and crash-risk measurement extends 12 months through three months after the fiscal-year-end. The initial CRSP–Compustat draw ends in 2007 and the paper says 2007 is its predictive-regression cutoff. The exact regression-year versus outcome-year convention and resulting final raw dates are unresolved; retain unknown upper endpoints for future-risk inputs.

The exact weekly return aggregation boundaries and fiscal-year mapping are not given. The expanded market model uses market-index leads/lags up to two weeks, and the source requires at least 26 weekly returns per fiscal year. Daily DSF/DSI fields are present, but a week-construction convention remains necessary.

The paper specifies a CRSP–Compustat intersection but not the CCM primary-link/type/overlap selection rule. CCM supplies candidate effective-dated identifiers; exact target-population linking remains unresolved.

The MB market-to-book ratio is not fully defined by numerator, denominator, adjustments or timing. The source also gives both beginning-year CSCORE characteristics and fiscal-year control definitions; the regression text says controls are at the beginning of t. An exact MB construction and alignment must be resolved.
The selected firm-fixed-effects baseline fit is reported, but the estimator used for that FE fit is not identified; OLS is specified only for comparison without firm fixed effects.

The Ball–Shivakumar sample excludes financial and utility firms, but the source does not define the SIC ranges or classification rule. Historical SICH is present, but exact sample mapping remains unresolved.

The paper’s Table 1 control definitions and the equation text differ on control timing: Table notes label most controls in fiscal year t, while the prose says all controls are measured at the beginning of year t. The temporal audit uses the explicit beginning-of-year statement for those controls and preserves the conflict.
Use current Compustat/CRSP vintages for the original paper period. Restated accounting fields, identifier histories and return-adjustment conventions may differ from the authors’ source vintage.

implementation_issues.description: The 1964–2007 period is reported for the predictive regressions/major variables, while CRASH and NCSKEW are t+1 outcomes and crash-risk measurement extends 12 months through three months after the fiscal-year-end. The initial CRSP–Compustat draw ends in 2007 and the paper says 2007 is its predictive-regression cutoff. The exact regression-year versus outcome-year convention and resulting final raw dates are unresolved; retain unknown upper endpoints for future-risk inputs.

The exact weekly return aggregation boundaries and fiscal-year mapping are not given. The expanded market model uses market-index leads/lags up to two weeks, and the source requires at least 26 weekly returns per fiscal year. Daily DSF/DSI fields are present, but a week-construction convention remains necessary.

The paper specifies a CRSP–Compustat intersection but not the CCM primary-link/type/overlap selection rule. CCM supplies candidate effective-dated identifiers; exact target-population linking remains unresolved.

The MB market-to-book ratio is not fully defined by numerator, denominator, adjustments or timing. The source also gives both beginning-year CSCORE characteristics and fiscal-year control definitions; the regression text says controls are at the beginning of t. An exact MB construction and alignment must be resolved.
The selected firm-fixed-effects baseline fit is reported, but the estimator used for that FE fit is not identified; OLS is specified only for comparison without firm fixed effects.

The Ball–Shivakumar sample excludes financial and utility firms, but the source does not define the SIC ranges or classification rule. Historical SICH is present, but exact sample mapping remains unresolved.

The paper’s Table 1 control definitions and the equation text differ on control timing: Table notes label most controls in fiscal year t, while the prose says all controls are measured at the beginning of year t. The temporal audit uses the explicit beginning-of-year statement for those controls and preserves the conflict.
Use current Compustat/CRSP vintages for the original paper period. Restated accounting fields, identifier histories and return-adjustment conventions may differ from the authors’ source vintage.
